title: SERVER IN SPACE MODULE FOR COMMUNICATION PAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.098) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Server in Space (SiS) module for regenerative processors in satellite communication systems, enablingefficienton-board data processing and offering advanced autonomy applications andemergency management services.TargetedImprovements: Enabling application layer processing on-board for Servers in Space to offer advanced autonomy applications and emergency management services.Description: It is expected that satellites will have a larger percentage of regenerative processing, which opens the door to application layer processing on-board of satellites. The mainchallenge to be addressed is the availability of a Server in Space (SiS) with application layer processing, with technical challenges to be addressed in terms of powerconsumption, radiation hardening of ground-based data centre technology, and maturity of application layersoftware for embedded devices. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: ON-BOARD 5G SPACE USER EQUIPMENT FOR LEO SATELLITES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.092) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, and demonstrate an on-board 5G space User Equipment (UE) for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites.Targeted Improvements:Provide a standardised method - leveraging 5G NTN developments - for broadband connectivity via data relay to LEO satellites.Description: The future 5G New Radio Non-Terrestrial Networks (5G NR NTN) will offer continuous and ubiquitous coverage targeting terrestrial user equipment.Through the New Space paradigm, a new group of users emerges in the form of LEO satellites such as CubeSats.The future 5G NTN networks (LEO/MEO/GEO) can be leveraged to provide standardised broadband connectivity services also to these space users for LEO. The gNodeBcan be either on the ground or in space. The activitywill- design and develop an on-board 5G space user equipment (UE) breadboard featuring the capabilities standardised in NTN.- identify a suitable mission for CubeSat with the developed breadboard embedded.- test and evaluate the connectivity performance level of the developed technology using a leased 5G NR NTN link.- implement and collect time-of-arrival measurements from NTN downlink signals used for communication.

title: M-IND - INDUSTRIALISATION OF MID-SIZE PLATFORMS FOR LEO CONSTELLATIONS (SAR OPTICAL)
description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation".  This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.
